slides.heading: Laptop Rentals
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Heaps
slides.narration: Let's solve Laptop Rentals, a hard heaps problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Given [start, end) rental intervals, minimum number of laptops needed so nobody waits.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Given start, end) rental intervals, minimum number of laptops needed so nobody waits.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The number of laptops needed equals the maximum number of overlapping rentals.
slides.narration: The number of laptops needed equals the maximum number of overlapping rentals.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Check overlaps for every pair → O(n²)
Sort by start + min-heap of end times → O(n log n)
slides.narration: Counting overlaps pairwise is quadratic. Sorting by start and keeping a min-heap of end times reuses the laptop that frees up earliest, in n log n.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 3. A start before the next end needs a laptop
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort starts and ends separately. Second, sweep with two pointers. Third, a start before the next end needs a laptop. Fourth, otherwise reuse one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [0, 2]: reuse
slides.narration: Interval 0 to 2: the earliest laptop is free by then, so reuse it. That's 1 in use.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [0, 4]: new laptop
slides.narration: Interval 0 to 4: no laptop is free yet, so we need another. That's 2 in use.

slides.narration: Interval 1 to 4: no laptop is free yet, so we need another. That's 3 in use.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We sort by start, and for each interval pop the heap if its earliest end is at most the start, then push the end. The heap size is the answer.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: A laptop returned at time t can be reused for a rental starting at t.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: The number of laptops needed equals the maximum number of overlapping rentals.
slides.narration: To recap Laptop Rentals: The number of laptops needed equals the maximum number of overlapping rentals. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
